contract.registration: A project supplies identity, revision, and generic capability declarations.
contract.intake: A task is admitted only with an exact project, task, lease, worktree, and session binding.
contract.capabilities: Required capabilities must be declared by both the project and the selected session.
contract.artifacts: Artifacts are exchanged through the AR-0087 namespaced, digest-verified registry.
contract.evidence: AWQ receives an opaque content-addressed evidence handoff; AWQ owns its meaning and acceptance.
contract.record_replay: Local deterministic requests may be recorded and replayed only on an exact request digest.
contract.terminal: Only one revision-bound terminal observation may be reconciled; success requires accepted evidence.

authority_boundaries.awc: owns identity, task revisions, claims, leases, and terminal authority
authority_boundaries.awr: consumes bindings, schedules boundary calls, routes artifacts, and projects evidence
authority_boundaries.awq: owns evidence policy and quality acceptance
authority_boundaries.awg: owns guidance and user-decision escalation when required
authority_boundaries.project: declares capabilities and supplies task inputs/results without changing runtime policy

invariants: Registration is idempotent only for an identical project identity and declaration.
Task intake rejects crossed project, tenant, project revision, task revision, lease, worktree, or session bindings.
The runtime consumes an existing scheduler lease and never creates a competing lease.
Required capabilities must be declared by the project and selected session.
Policy references are opaque digests and are never interpreted by the runtime.
Artifacts use the AR-0087 project/worktree namespace and immutable content/provenance digests.
AWQ evidence handoff requires an existing artifact and exact runtime binding.
Authority outcomes other than the versioned finite result set fail closed.
A replay with changed request, binding, revision, or evidence is rejected.
A successful terminal requires the exact evidence digest previously handed to AWQ.
Missing, stale, or contradictory terminal observations never become approval.
A terminal observation is immutable and idempotent only for an identical observation.
The runtime does not embed application-specific policy or provider credentials.
No network, provider, or LLM execution is required by this contract.
